```{r}
#| label: library
#| include: false
options(housepi.footer.warranty = TRUE)
options(housepi.footer.sample = TRUE)
library(housepi)
housepi_theme_set()
set.seed(42)
```

Certain models allow for the definition of custom group rates.
Such models allow for a number of group rates which can then be changed according to the modeler's choice.
We provide an example here with the heterogeneous version of the final size model.

# Format data features

Suppose our analysis wants to explore age and/or gender-based effects within a household survey.
We start by creating categorical groupings to stratify individuals based on their age, sex, etc. and then associate individual group rates.

```{r}
#| label: format-age-data

# define a model object with a subset of the SarsCoV-2 (ICoFs) data
hhmodel <- sarscov2_2021_icofs |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    # change age in survey as a binary group child/adult
    age = dplyr::case_when(age < 19 ~ "child", .default = "adult")
  ) |> 
  # use smaller number of households for exploration
  dplyr::filter(house_id %in% sample(unique(house_id), 300)) |>
  new_housepi_model("case_ascertained")
```

The current loaded model allows for a number of group rates, among which the individual `"susceptibility"` (use `help()` method to learn more).
We can define it calling `add_group_rate()`.
By default, all group rates without a definition will be treated as associated to the reference (i.e. `1`). Definitions will add a new parameter for each group, except for the reference group.
By default, the definition assumes the reference group to be the one with the largest number of counts.

```{r}
#| label: susceptibility-by-age
hhmodel |>
  # associate susceptibility group rate by column age
  add_group_rate("susceptibility", by = "age") |>
  # inspect group rate definitions
  # note: to show group rate definitions, add data before
  get_group_rates()
```
To return a group rate to its default, overwrite its definition with argument `by` set to `NA`.
To drop all previous definitions, add a new one with `append = FALSE`.

# Dependencies between covariates

In the previous example we associated group rates to a single covariate in the data.
In this example we show how to provide more covariates and a custom reference.
Manually set a `reference` by providing the corresponding group factor values:

```{r}
#| label: susceptibility-by-sex-age
hhmodel |>
  # multiplicative group rates, adult female chosen as reference
  add_group_rate("susceptibility", c("sex", "age"),
                 reference = c(sex = "F", age = "adult")) |>
  # show corresponding tables with associations
  get_group_rates()
```

By default, parameters associated to each grouping are assumed independent,
i.e. the group rate is the product of two parameters, one for the feature "sex", another for "age".
In alternative, we can make the rate joint between the features:

```{r}
#| label: susceptibility-joint
hhmodel |>
  # here covariates are assumed to be joint
  add_group_rate("susceptibility", c("sex", "age"),
                 reference = c(sex = "F", age = "adult"),
                 joint = TRUE) |>
  get_group_rates()
```

# Parameters associated to rates

To perform inference of the parameters associated to each group we just need to provide options for the Bayesian Monte Carlo.
By default, group rate assumes lognormal prior (`meanlog = 0` and `sdlog = 3`) and lognormal proposal, following @cauchemez_household_2009.
This can be customized at the moment of the definition of the group rate similarly to parameters (see documentation).

```{r}
#| label: group-rate-parameters
# default parameter associated to group rates
hhmodel |>
  add_group_rate("susceptibility", c("sex", "age"), prefix = "") |>
  get_parameters()

# custom parameter priors associated to group rates
hhmodel |>
  add_group_rate("susceptibility", c("sex", "age"), prefix = "",
                 prior = "normal") |>
  get_parameters()

```

Note that direct definition of a parameter has the priority, even if a parameter with the same name would be generated by group rate application.

# Inference with group rates

We can proceed with the inference as shown in [Get started](housepi.html):

```{r}
#| label: final-group-rates

hhmodel <- hhmodel |>
  # load group rates from definition list
  add_group_rate(
    infectivity = "isolated",
    susceptibility = list(by = "vacc_status", reference = "unvaccinated")
  )

# show parameter definitions used for the inference
get_parameters(hhmodel)
```


```{r}
#| label: inference-group-rates
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Six trace plots displaying MCMC sampling behaviour for model parameters: alpha, beta, infectivity by isolation, and susceptibility parameters stratified by vaccination status.
#|  Multiple chains (1-3) are overlaid across iterations, showing convergence diagnostics and mixing properties of the Markov chains.

test_delay <- 8
hhmodel <- hhmodel |>
  add_house_observ(start_date = min(test_date@D)) |> 
  # parameter definitions
  add_parameter(
    alpha = list(prior = "uniform", proposal = "lognormal"),
    beta = list(prior = "uniform", proposal = "lognormal"),
    gamma = list(prior = "uniform", proposal = "uniform", max = 5),
    hhsize_ref = 5
  ) |>
  # augmented definitions
  add_augmented(
    # public definitions
    infec_time = list(
      prior = "uniform", loc = start_date@D, min = -8, max = study_period@D
    ),
    # accessory generic definitions
    .incub_period = list(prior = "gamma", mean = 3, var = 2),
    .onset_time = infec_time + .incub_period,
  ) |>
  # observation model
  add_observation(
    #> symptomatic (status = 1)
    test_date = list(
      status = 1, discr = TRUE, obs = "normal",
      mean = .onset_time, sd = 1, min = floor(.onset_time)
    ),
    #> asymptomatic (status = 2)
    test_date = list(
      status = 2, discr = TRUE, obs = "uniform",
      loc = ceil(infec_time), min = 0, max = 8
    )
  ) |>
  # infectivity profile definitions
  # FIXME: this needs to be clarified
  add_infec_profile("gamma", mean = 4, var = 2.5)

# perform inference
results <- hhmodel |>
  run_inference(progress = 4)

bayesplot::mcmc_trace(get_parameter_draws(results))
```

# Compare group rates

Finally, we propose the following approach to visualize the difference between the estimates for the susceptibility with respect to the reference group:

```{r}
#| label: compare-group-rates-plot
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-alt: >
#|  Posterior estimates of relative susceptibility by age-sex groups (adult male, child female, child male) with reference to adult females.
#|  Points show mean estimates with 95% credible intervals derived from MCMC posterior distributions.
library(ggplot2)

rate_id <- "susceptibility"
prefix <- "sus_"

tmp <- get_group_rates(hhmodel) |>
  # extract reference value and create a label
  dplyr::filter(group_rate == rate_id, param_name == ".reference") |>
  dplyr::select(vacc_status)
ylabel <- sprintf("%s (Ref: %s)", rate_id,
                  paste(paste(names(tmp), tmp, sep = " "), collapse = " "))

# compare inferred susceptibility group rates
results |>
  summarise_draws() |>
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_starts(variable, prefix)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(get_group_rates(hhmodel) |>
                     dplyr::select(param_name, n) |>
                     dplyr::rename(variable = param_name),
                   by = "variable") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    variable = stringr::str_remove(variable, "sus_vacc_status") |> 
      stringr::str_replace_all("_", " ")
    ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = variable, y = median, label = sprintf("[%s]", n))) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = "black") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(nudge_x = 0.2, nudge_y = 0.1, color = "coral") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = q2.5, ymax = q97.5)) +
  labs(x = "", y = ylabel)
```
